explain.say: Two partners shape almost every landscape on Earth: weathering and erosion. They often work together, but they are not the same thing.

explain.say: Weathering breaks rock down where it is, without moving it. Physical weathering cracks rock, like frost or roots; chemical weathering changes it, like acidic rain dissolving limestone.

explain.say: Erosion picks up the broken pieces and carries them away. Rivers, waves, wind, glaciers and gravity are the movers.

explain.say: Eventually the moving material is dropped somewhere else, which is called deposition. Together, weathering, erosion and deposition carve valleys, build beaches and wear mountains down.

faq.q: What is the difference between weathering and erosion?
faq.a: Weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces where it sits. Erosion is the moving of those pieces away by water, wind, ice or gravity.

faq.q: What are the types of weathering?
faq.a: Physical weathering breaks rock without changing it, such as freeze-thaw and roots. Chemical weathering changes the minerals, such as acid rain dissolving limestone or iron rusting. Biological weathering is caused by living things.
Moving water is the biggest cause, along with waves, wind, glaciers and gravity pulling material downhill.
asks: What are the agents of erosion?

faq.a: Deposition is when moving water, wind or ice slows down and drops the material it carried, building beaches, deltas, dunes and new sedimentary layers.
Roots grow into cracks in rock and slowly force them apart as they thicken. Lichens and mosses also release chemicals that weaken rock surfaces.

facts: Running water is the main agent of erosion on land.
Chemical weathering is fastest in warm, wet climates.

quiz.say: A river carries pebbles downstream. Is that weathering or erosion?
quiz.why: Erosion is the carrying away of broken rock, and the river is doing the carrying.

wrong.1: Weathering breaks rock in place; it does not move it.
wrong.2: Deposition is when the river drops the pebbles, not while it carries them.
